storyboard.claim: Dark romance makes you root for the dangerous man; your heartbeat sinks with the protagonist.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray beside Avery, a heart marking the physiological pull the narration names.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cold open.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names who 'him' is before the narration finishes making the point.

storyboard.claim: By page 50 you can't tell if you're afraid or aroused, and that's the point.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum balanced dead-center between the two named feelings.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes the confusion from beat 0 literal and measurable.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the two poles as equally weighted, not one bleeding into the other.

storyboard.claim: The book forces an uncomfortable question right out of the gate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery caught mid-thought, unresolved.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates beat 1's confusion as a question instead of a feeling.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: mostly host filler ('right', 'incredibly uncomfortable') with no new content yet.

storyboard.claim: Why do we enjoy watching someone walk into a trap?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The mirror reflecting the viewer back — a meta question about why audiences enjoy watching someone walk into a trap.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the difficult question into its concrete image: a trap being walked into.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the abstract 'question' a literal shape the viewer can see.

storyboard.claim: The viewer is someone who likes examining how captivating things actually work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader-stand-in holding a magnifier over the material.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the viewer's own analytical stance after setting up the trap.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: describes the show's own approach, not the book's content.

storyboard.claim: Today's mission: run Steph Macca's Unhinged through a different analytical filter.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader-stand-in holding the novel itself.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the specific book the machinery-pulling-apart from beat 4 will be applied to.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: pure show-framing, no plot or claim content yet.

storyboard.claim: We're not treating this as edgy fiction — it's a meticulously constructed psychological case study.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clinical case file standing in for the book's proposed treatment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Declares the analytical frame that beat 5's book will be read through.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the clinical register the rest of the video will use.

storyboard.claim: Avery has just been placed in the Lilyale Foundation Center, marketed as a high-society psychiatric facility.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery arriving at the psychiatric facility.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the show's framing to the actual story: the subject and the environment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds the case study in a physical place before the 'gilded prison' reveal.

storyboard.claim: Marketed as luxury treatment on paper, Lilyale actually operates like a gilded prison.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery bound within the institution's walls.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Corrects the 'high security facility' label from beat 7 with what it really is.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the contrast between marketing and reality visible, not just stated.

storyboard.claim: Avery's emotional architecture has been completely hollowed out by catastrophic prior trauma.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery with a vast hidden depth beneath her surface.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the prison setting to what the prison holds: an already-damaged person.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals there is more beneath Avery than the setting alone shows.

storyboard.claim: The architect who steps into that hollowed-out space is a fellow inmate, Gray, who is deeply dangerous.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray reaching toward Avery's hollowed-out space from beat 9.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Fills the hollow space named in beat 9 with the person who will exploit it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts a face on the threat instead of leaving it abstract.

storyboard.claim: Gray doesn't seduce Avery despite her wounds — that's the wrong reading, corrected next beat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray reaching toward Avery's scars.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the thesis promised in beat 10 as a claim about to be corrected.
storyboard.addedInformation: Struck through to flag it as the framing the next beat rejects.

storyboard.claim: He seduces her through her wounds, not despite them — the power dynamic is never symmetrical.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray towering over Avery in a low angle, sized to their imbalance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Corrects the struck 'despite her wounds' from beat 11 with the real mechanism.
storyboard.addedInformation: The camera angle itself shows the asymmetry, not just the caption.

storyboard.claim: Macca never pretends the dynamic is equal — this is a precision study of the nervous system, not a love story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery held in the same clinical, examined framing as the case-study beats.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the genre label ('love story') the book is refusing, after showing why in beat 12.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: restates the case-study framing from beat 6 rather than adding new content.

storyboard.claim: The book examines how trauma, isolation, and behavioral conditioning rewire a person's nervous system.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery marked with the electric rewiring the narration names.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns 'precision study' from beat 13 into its specific subject: the rewired nervous system.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes 'rewired' a visible event on her, not just a phrase.

storyboard.claim: A specific behavioral conditioning tactic, intermittent reinforcement, can alter a person's biological survival instincts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Skinner box — the exact mechanism the narration names.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the specific mechanism behind the 'rewiring' introduced in beat 14.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the abstract conditioning tactic its literal experimental apparatus.

storyboard.claim: The book is like a haunted house where the architect hands you the blueprints himself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray holding out the blueprint-like documents.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the Skinner-box mechanism from beat 15 as a haunted-house metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: Casts Gray as the one openly showing his own trap.

storyboard.claim: You're handed the blueprints right at the front door — you see the trap doors, the trip wires.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery examining the visible blueprint of the trap she is about to walk into anyway.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Places the blueprints from beat 16 at their literal delivery point, the door.
storyboard.addedInformation: Anchors the metaphor to one concrete threshold instead of staying abstract.

storyboard.claim: You know the floor will give out, and you walk inside and step on the trip wires anyway.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The floor fracturing under Avery's steps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pays off the trip wires named at the door in beat 17 with the floor actually giving way.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the breaking point is walked into knowingly, not by accident.

storyboard.claim: To understand how Avery is dismantled, look at how she was built first — she is not a blank slate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery alone, already carrying weight before Gray enters.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from the haunted-house metaphor of beats 16-18 back to Avery's own history.
storyboard.addedInformation: Struck through: the narration explicitly rejects the 'blank slate' framing.

storyboard.claim: Her medical file, discussed by staff with alarming casualness, outlines a massive history of damage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dr. Smith reading Avery's file with clinical detachment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the 'not a blank slate' claim from beat 19 its documented proof: the file.
storyboard.addedInformation: The staff's detachment is shown, not just described.

storyboard.claim: She has extensive physical scars — burn marks severe enough to require a skin graft.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The burn scars on Avery's arm, named directly by the narration.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Specifies the first item in the file opened in beat 20.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the exact physical evidence on screen instead of a generic file.

storyboard.claim: Her back is heavily scarred from a beer bottle attack that required surgery to remove the glass.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery slumped, carrying the second, older injury named in the file.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds a second, separate wound to the burn scars named in beat 21.
storyboard.addedInformation: Confirms the damage is plural and pre-existing, not a single incident.

storyboard.claim: Beyond broken bones, Dr. Smith confirms she's been formally diagnosed with borderline personality disorder.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dr. Smith delivering the formal diagnosis from her file.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from physical scars (beats 21-22) to the psychiatric diagnosis in the same file.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: mostly a list item ('broken bones') folded into the surrounding diagnosis beat.

storyboard.claim: The hosts pause: fiction often gets a diagnosis like this wrong.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader-stand-in stepping back from Avery's file to comment on the genre.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Breaks from Avery's specific diagnosis in beat 23 to a genre-wide critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: Flags that a meta-commentary segment is starting before the payoff in beat 27.

storyboard.claim: Usually a diagnosis is just an excuse for erratic behavior or a lazy exposition-heavy backstory dump.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader-stand-in continuing the genre critique from beat 24.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the specific bad habit the critique in beat 24 was pointing at.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the vague 'gets this wrong' a concrete named failure mode.

callout.text: SITS IN A CHAIR AND MONOLOGUES

storyboard.claim: The cliché: a character just sits in a chair and monologues about their sad past like a therapy session.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery seated, staged as the cliché therapy-monologue scene being described.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Dramatizes the 'lazy backstory dump' named in beat 25 as a literal scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows exactly what the criticized cliché looks like, set up to be contrasted next.

storyboard.claim: Macca avoids the cliché — she writes the trauma somatically, entirely through Avery's bodily responses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery's physical reaction standing in for the monologue that isn't given.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the chair-and-monologue cliché from beat 26 with what Macca does instead.
storyboard.addedInformation: Corrects the cliché rather than just naming the alternative in the abstract.

callout.text: NOT JUST LABELS ON HER CHART

storyboard.claim: BPD and PTSD aren't just labels on her chart — they're the lens her nervous system processes everything through.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery's file from beat 20, now struck through as an incomplete explanation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Circles back to the chart from beat 20 to reject reading it as the whole story.
storyboard.addedInformation: Struck through: the narration explicitly negates 'just labels on her chart'.

storyboard.claim: Let's unpack the neurobiology of chronic, inescapable trauma like Avery's.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dr. Smith pointing into the abstract nervous-system space.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the 'lens' claim from beat 28 into the specific science segment that follows.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a transition line promising detail delivered in the next beat.

storyboard.claim: Chronic trauma leaves the amygdala, the brain's threat detector, stuck in the on position.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery marked with the same electric charge as the earlier 'rewired' beat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the specific brain structure behind the neurobiology promised in beat 29.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives 'rewired' (beat 14) its specific mechanism: an amygdala that won't switch off.

storyboard.claim: She's perpetually scanning for a threat that isn't necessarily there — hypervigilance feels like normal to her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery scanning her surroundings under the magnifier's focus.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the behavior the 'stuck on' amygdala from beat 30 actually produces.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes hypervigilance a visible, constant activity rather than a diagnosis word.

storyboard.claim: Live in a war zone long enough, and the sudden absence of gunfire doesn't make you feel relaxed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery tense even in stillness, contradicting the expected calm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the scanning in beat 31 never stops, even without a visible threat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Struck through: the narration explicitly negates the expected relief.

storyboard.claim: When Gray casually touches her leg, she flinches violently — her brain assumes the predator is just hiding.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery recoiling the instant Gray touches her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the abstract paranoia from beat 32 its first concrete scene in the story.
storyboard.addedInformation: Turns the theory of hypervigilance into an actual moment between the two leads.

storyboard.claim: Alone with Theo, when he reaches for her wrist to cover her scars with a tattoo, she is absolutely terrified.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Theo's tattoo machine reaching toward Avery's bandaged wrist.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Repeats the flinch pattern from beat 33 with a different, gentler man.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the fear reaction isn't specific to Gray — it's her baseline with anyone.

storyboard.claim: She trembles because her baseline assumption is that violence is always coming.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery trembling, the aftermath of Theo's approach in beat 34.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the physical detail underneath the terror shown in beat 34.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: restates 'terrified' from beat 34 with a slightly more specific physical word.

storyboard.claim: A common critique of dark romance: these books use trauma as a cheap accessory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader-stand-in raising the genre critique, echoing beats 24-25.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from Avery's own scenes back to the genre-level pushback promised earlier.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the specific criticism beat 38 will go on to refute.

storyboard.claim: Give the female lead a tragic backstory just to make her edgy and give the bad boy something to fix.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery staged as the object of the trope being described.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the exact mechanism behind the 'cheap accessory' critique from beat 36.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the trope's condescension visible by staging Avery as its object.

storyboard.claim: The 'I can fix her' trope doesn't apply here — Macca isn't using the trauma as an accessory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery and Gray together, rejecting the fix-her trope named in beat 37.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Directly refutes the critique staged in beats 36-37.
storyboard.addedInformation: Struck through: the narration explicitly negates 'as an accessory'.

storyboard.claim: Trauma is the foundational architecture of the trap — Gray is establishing the exact combination code to Avery's vault.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray reading Avery like a lock he's learning to open.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the refuted 'accessory' critique (beat 38) as what trauma actually is: the trap's architecture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Turns 'trauma as accessory' into 'trauma as the exact mechanism of the trap', setting up beat 40's predator payoff.
